title: Three-Dimensional Map of Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty Detachment: Development and Application of a Deep Learning Model.
summary: The model quantified graft detachment area and volume and was more sensitive than slit-lamp estimates in some substantial detachments; mean percent detachment exceeded specialists’ estimates by 8.2 percentage points (95% CI 6.2–10.2). Separate validation set: 20 scans/5,120 labeled images, Youden index 0.85, Dice 0.73 and R² 0.90 against manual labels. A prospective application set included 107 eyes; masked re-review of discrepant scans supported cases where clinicians underestimated detachment. No clinical outcome benefit was tested.
ai_technology: A supervised neural network segments posterior cornea and detached graft in anterior-segment OCT slices; the 3D maps aggregate the resulting cross-sectional segmentation.
organization: Eye Center, Albert-Ludwigs-University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany

source_review.scope: Read the primary full paper (publisher PDF copy via the University of Freiburg repository), including Methods and Results; checked both frozen catalogs for title/result duplicates. A U-Net segmentation model maps DMEK graft detachment from anterior-segment OCT, with separate manually labeled training and validation sets; the model was also applied to 107 prospectively followed eyes and identified detachments that clinicians underestimated. This is a specific clinical imaging result, not evidence of improved patient outcomes.
